title: How to Get Into Berghain - Quick Summary
items: **The door is selective, not random.** Berghain, a former power plant in Friedrichshain, has a hard door run by Sven Marquardt's team. There is no dress code list and no guaranteed way in, but how you behave genuinely shifts your odds. Nothing gets you turned away faster than a big, loud group.

**What helps at the door:** come solo or in a small group, stay calm and quiet in the queue, dress dark and plain, know who is playing, and bring ID (18-plus). Do not film, do not be visibly drunk, and never argue if you are turned away.

**The bigger mistake is arriving too early.** Berlin has had no legal closing time since 1949, so there is no last call to beat. Turning up at 22:00 means queueing for an empty room. Floors fill after 01:00 to 02:00, the peak runs from about 03:00 to well past 08:00, and Sunday-daytime dancing is completely normal.

**Money and rules:** entry to a Klubnacht is roughly 25 to 30 euros. Card now works at the door and the bars since late 2025, but the cloakroom is still cash, so bring some. Phones get a sticker over the camera inside; the no-photo rule is core to the culture.

**If Berghain is not your night,** try friendlier doors: Sisyphos (festival-like, Rummelsburg), Kater Blau on the Spree at Holzmarkt, ://about blank (Friedrichshain, queer-friendly), Tresor (historic techno in the Kraftwerk building) or RSO (Schöneweide). Watergate closed at the end of 2024, so ignore older guides.

**Getting there:** Berghain is a couple of minutes from Ostbahnhof (S-Bahn and regional trains). The U-Bahn and S-Bahn run all night on Friday and Saturday, with night buses the rest of the week, so getting home late is easy.
